rooms.title: The Parcel Depot

sources.label: Nell’s note bag
sources.hint: Talk to Nell to receive eight note tiles. They open musical locks. This bag is separate from the returned letter.

sources.label: The small delivery chest
sources.hint: Nell points out a small chest beside her counter. Its half note is needed for every opening door.

doors.label: The garden door
doors.hint: Hold a sound for two beats, then leave two beats silent.

doors.label: The workshop door
doors.hint: Hold for two beats. Then play two eighth notes and four sixteenth notes.

doors.label: The canal door
doors.hint: Hold for two beats, play one quarter note, then two eighth notes.

doors.label: The town-link door
doors.hint: Hold for two beats, play one quarter note, then two eighth notes. Save every other starting note for the two locks ahead.

rooms.description: The bell is silent. Mira and her friends follow a returned letter to learn why mail, water, and ferry checks have stopped.

rooms.title: Iris’s Garden Porch

sources.label: Iris’s garden notes
sources.hint: Talk to Iris for a half note and a half rest. They replace the tiles used at the first garden door.

doors.label: The overgrown arch
doors.warning: Iris warns that the arch is blocked. Its service route costs an extra four-beat key.

rooms.description: Iris asks Mira to listen to the space between notes. Her gift is claimed once through conversation.

sources.label: Pip’s workshop notes
sources.hint: Talk to Pip for a half note, paired eighths, and four sixteenths. The next workshop door needs these notes.

doors.label: The silent aviary
doors.warning: The quiet aviary is a detour. Its service gate costs another four beats, so save the notes needed at the final lock.

sources.label: The stamped delivery chest
sources.hint: Oren points out a chest with Nell’s postage stamp. Its three notes fit the next canal door.

doors.label: The empty ferry
doors.warning: Oren warns that no boat waits beyond this door.

rooms.title: The Overgrown Arch

doors.label: The garden service gate
doors.hint: Hold a sound for two beats, then leave two beats silent. This extra gate spends four beats before the garden fork.
doors.warning: The final garden door still needs its own four-beat key.

rooms.description: The arch is blocked, but an older southern service gate reaches the garden paths. Its extra key spends notes that may be needed later.

doors.label: The hearth path
doors.hint: A dotted half note lasts three beats. Add a quarter note to reach the homes.

doors.label: The old stone path
doors.hint: Try the two one-beat groups, a quarter rest, a single eighth, and paired sixteenths.

rooms.title: The Silent Aviary

doors.label: The workshop service gate
doors.hint: Hold for two beats, then play two eighth notes and four sixteenth notes. The service gate spends another four beats.
doors.warning: The final workshop door still needs the dotted half note and quarter note.

rooms.description: The quiet bird room has an older southern service gate to the workshop paths. Taking it costs an extra four-beat key.

doors.label: The schoolroom stair
doors.hint: Use a three-beat dotted half note and a quarter note to reach the music room.

doors.label: The birds’ back passage
doors.hint: Play a single eighth and paired sixteenths. Then use a half rest and a quarter rest.

doors.label: The town-bell stair
doors.hint: Use a three-beat dotted half note, then four sixteenth notes, to climb toward the bell.

doors.label: The copied waterway
doors.warning: Oren’s map shows that this channel reaches an extra paid service stair. The bell still needs its own four-beat key.

doors.label: The home door
doors.hint: Use the five tiles you brought: two eighths, four sixteenths, a quarter rest, a single eighth, and paired sixteenths.

doors.label: The music-room door
doors.hint: Play a single eighth and paired sixteenths for beat one. A half rest and a quarter rest finish the rhythm.

rooms.title: The Copied Waterway

doors.label: The bell service stair
doors.hint: Hold for three beats, then play four sixteenth notes. The service stair spends four beats to reach the bell controls.
doors.warning: The bell still needs a separate four-beat answer after this stair.

rooms.description: The channel ends at a wall, but the southern service stair reaches the bell controls. That extra gate spends the four beats needed at the bell.

doors.label: The town door
doors.hint: Play a single eighth and paired sixteenths for beat one. Then leave two beats silent and one more silent.

rooms.title: The Overgrown Music Box

sources.label: Four notes under the flower stone
sources.hint: Look for a stone carved with a flower. Inspect it, then Search for four notes and a hidden gate.

doors.label: The hidden flower gate
doors.hint: The four new one-beat tiles from the flower stone open this gate.

rooms.description: The hidden pickup is inside the chosen secret branch. It cannot be collected on the normal path and cannot leak into a regular ending.

rooms.title: The Birds’ Dusty Attic

sources.label: Two notes inside the hollow perch
sources.hint: Inspect the hollow bird perch, then Search. Its hidden half note and half rest reveal another gate.

doors.label: The hidden brass gate
doors.hint: A half note sounds for two beats. A half rest leaves two beats silent.

rooms.description: Searching is optional before choosing this detour. Inside it, the once-only hidden cache is needed for the only forward gate; it remains available until found.

doors.label: The unfinished-song door
doors.hint: Use the dotted half note and quarter note you saved for this last door.

doors.label: The birds’ answer door
doors.hint: Use the dotted half note and quarter note you saved through the hidden passage.

rooms.title: The Meeting of Routes

doors.label: The shared-signal gate
doors.hint: Hold a sound for three beats, then play four sixteenth notes.

rooms.description: The old service routes meet here. What the group learned on every earlier route lets them connect the homes, school, water clocks, and courier birds in one run.

rooms.title: The Listening Heart

doors.label: The answering-bell door
doors.hint: Play a single eighth and paired sixteenths for beat one. A half rest and quarter rest leave room for the town’s reply.

rooms.description: The bell must wait for separate replies instead of treating every voice as an echo. This final key uses the last four starting notes.

terminals.title: The Empty Ferry
terminals.repair: Start a new run. Open the stamped chest in the canal storehouse, then choose the delivery gate.

rules: Doors accept their authored ordered recipe, not every rhythm of equal duration. Every door costs exactly four beats. Incorrect answers spend nothing.

All sources are explicit interactions, claimed once globally per run. Entering a room awards no notes automatically. Starting a new run resets supplies while preserving learned clues and explored routes.

Nell supplies eight kinds worth ten beats; the depot chest holds the missing half note worth two beats. Every opening door needs that half note and another two beats, so both starting sources are required.
A branch’s once-only gift or chest restores the kinds spent at its opening door. The direct porch gate therefore requires collecting that supply before leaving.
Every paid door is irreversible during the run. Undo edits only the uncommitted rhythm answer. No return gate refunds notes or restores already-claimed supplies.
The overgrown arch, quiet aviary, and copied-waterway doors are explicit risk entries. Their service gates add a four-beat cost that can consume the final key or leave the wrong note types.
Hidden caches require explicit searching. Each supplies its own four-beat hidden gate, so finding a cache does not replace a final key spent on an earlier detour.

Successful endings use zero of every note kind. A nonterminal room with no affordable revealed door and no unclaimed local source ends the run: an empty bag is out of notes, and a nonempty unusable bag lacks the right types.
A failed run keeps its discovered rooms, connections, and clues. Restart begins at the depot with an empty bag and fresh once-only supplies; journal knowledge never grants current-run notes.

The verifier accepts only witnessed resource losses whose every history crossed a declared risk-entry door. Unmarked blocked states, broken success balances, unreachable content, and ungated secret endings still fail.

The town-link door at the depot opens only after all eleven earlier outcomes are recorded, including both secret endings and all six failed-run outcomes. Its two inner gates use the remaining starting notes. Journal progress unlocks the route but never supplies notes.
Progress-gated content is proved with both a fresh journal and all required outcomes. Content intentionally locked before completion is reported separately; full-progress coverage remains strict.

budgetProof.regular: 12 initial beats + 4 branch-source beats = 4 doors × 4 beats = 16; zero remains.
budgetProof.secret: 12 initial + 4 branch-source + 4 hidden-cache beats = 5 doors × 4 beats = 20; zero remains.
budgetProof.typed: Each safe branch keeps its two original four-beat vectors. Direct routes spend A then B; secret routes spend B, their separate hidden-cache vector, then A.
budgetProof.canalLoss: The copied-waterway route pays its extra service stair: 16 supplied beats are spent before the last bell door, which still needs another four beats. The bag reaches zero at the bell controls.
budgetProof.gardenAndWorkshopLoss: Taking the risky porch door spends the original final key. Its service gate then spends the branch gift. The hidden cache pays only its own gate, leaving zero notes before the secret final door.
budgetProof.missingTypes: Skipping the porch gift and choosing its risky door leaves four beats of other types. The extra service gate cannot be paid, so the attempt ends without a refund.
budgetProof.runHistories: Fresh journals retain 43 reachable states, 43 transitions, 14 terminal histories, and 10 resource-loss histories: 24 complete runs. With all eleven prior outcomes recorded, the three-door ultimate route adds three states, three transitions, and two supply-order histories: 46 states, 46 transitions, and 26 complete runs.
budgetProof.ultimate: 12 initial beats = C (half, quarter, paired eighths) + A (dotted half, four sixteenths) + B (single eighth, paired sixteenths, half rest, quarter rest) = 3 doors × 4 beats; zero of every note kind remains. No extra supplies are awarded.
